newsitem.title: PERU: Peru exec says Lehman buys 50 pct of sugar grower.
newsitem.headline: Peru exec says Lehman buys 50 pct of sugar grower.

text.p: Businessman Genaro Delgado Parker on Friday said he sold his 50 percent stake in Peruvian sugar grower Agro Industrial Paramonga SA to Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc.

The deal, which has been "signed, sealed and delivered," gives Lehman a stake in a major Peruvian agricultural concern and allows Delgado to concentrate on his stakes in local television and telecommunications, he said.
"By selling my shares, I am getting out of the agriculture sector completely. I'm not a farmer," he told Reuters.

Technically, Delgado sold his shares of Paramonga's holding company, Rio Pativilca, which owned 74 percent of Paramonga before the deal. About 13 percent of Paramonga is owned by workers, and businessman Jaime Mur owns most of the rest, Delgado said.

Delgado declined to give financial details except to say the company was profitable and that the $25 million purchase cited by a Lima newspaper was "in the right area." He declined to provide the company's production figures.
Delgado said he retained a token stock participation after the deal but that he planned to sell that as well.

Paramonga, with extensive sugar holdings on the Pacific coast north of Lima, was a state-owned cooperative until it was put in private hands with a large share of worker ownership about four years ago.
Owned by the WR Grace Inc of the United States until it was nationalized in the early 1970s, Paramonga bears no relation to the state-owned Paramonga papermaker nearby.
